title: Cold-open hook
find: hook opening first seconds title card reveal
body: Start on the single strongest sentence of the footage (a question, a surprising claim, the payoff) and cut the warm-up. The first 1-3 seconds decide whether a stranger stops scrolling. Reorder segments freely: the strongest line may sit late in the footage. Watch out: the line must stay true to what the speaker meant; never open on a promise the rest of the ad does not support.

title: Pattern-interrupt opening
find: punch zoom whoosh impact glitch first frame
body: Break the scroll rhythm in the first second with something unexpected: a fast punch-in, a hard cut, a sound hit, a bold text slam. Use it once, at the open, not as constant decoration. Pair with a strong first line; the interrupt earns attention, the line keeps it.

title: Open loop (ask, then delay the answer)
find: question tension reveal beat
body: Pose the question or tease the result first, then take the viewer through the reasoning before paying it off. Works well for explainers and trading education. The payoff must arrive inside the ad, or the loop feels like bait.

title: Problem, agitate, solution
find: problem solution structure narrative arc
body: Name the pain the viewer already feels, make it concrete, then present the way out. A reliable arc for cold audiences. Keep each beat short: one sentence of pain, one of consequence, then the solution.

title: Show the proof, then make the claim
find: chart data stat number evidence
body: Put the evidence on screen (a chart, a number the speaker states, a screenshot of the method) before or as the claim lands. Builds trust and survives compliance review better than a bare promise. Only show numbers that are spoken in the ad.

title: One clear action to finish
find: call to action end card button outro
body: End on exactly one action, said and shown (what to tap, what happens next). The closing card is the last few seconds; keep it uncluttered and legible. Vary its design with the ad, but never change the owner's required wording.

title: Jump-cut pacing (trim dead air)
find: trim silence pause cut remove filler
body: Remove pauses longer than about half a second, leaving a sliver of air so speech still sounds natural, and drop filler starts (so, and, um). Keeps energy up in talking-head footage. Too tight sounds robotic: leave beats before key lines.

title: Cut on breaths and word boundaries
find: cut point edge audio waveform silence
body: Place every cut in the quietest moment between words, never mid-syllable, and start and end segments on whole sentences. Clean edges are the difference between a pro cut and a glitchy one. Re-listen to each edge after cutting.

title: J-cut and L-cut
find: audio overlap crossfade split edit transition
body: Let the next line's audio start before its picture (J-cut) or the last line's audio run over the next picture (L-cut). Smooths joins between segments and hides the edit. Needs separate audio and video timing; check lip-sync stays natural.

title: Punch-in on the key word
find: scale zoom keyframes push in crop emphasis
body: A quick scale-up of 5-15% when a key word lands, held until the next beat, simulates a second camera and re-engages attention. Alternate between two or three framings in long takes. Do not zoom constantly and keep captions and faces inside safe zones while scaled.

title: Speed ramp for emphasis
find: speed ramp setpts atempo slow motion time remap
body: Briefly speed up transitions or slow a key moment. Speech must keep its pitch and clarity, so use it on b-roll or silent beats, rarely on talking. Easy to overdo.

title: Leave a beat after the key line
find: pause beat silence hold
body: After the line that matters, hold half a second (or add a small graphic hit) before moving on. Contrast with tight pacing elsewhere makes the key line land.

title: Word-by-word captions
find: captions words highlight karaoke subtitle word timing
body: Show 1-3 words at a time, timed to the speech, large and high-contrast. Most viewers watch muted. Group by pause and length, keep to about 16 characters per line, and make every caption word match what is said: accuracy beats style.

title: Highlight the key word
find: highlight pill color emphasis word underline
body: Colour, enlarge or box one important word per sentence (a number, the idea word). Draws the eye to what matters. Overuse turns the whole caption into noise.

title: Keep captions in the safe zone
find: safe zone layout bottom margin ui overlap reels stories
body: Vertical placements cover the bottom and top of the frame with interface (buttons, profile, caption). Keep important text away from roughly the top 14% and bottom 20-25%, and away from the speaker's face.

title: Adapt caption colour to the footage
find: contrast luminance color text background legibility
body: Measure the brightness behind the caption band and choose light-on-dark or dark-on-light, with an outline or shadow when the background is busy. Fixed colours fail on bright or dim footage.

title: Kinetic headline
find: kinetic type text animation headline title reveal
body: Animate the headline in with purpose: words arrive on the beat of the speech, one idea per line, large weight contrast. Keep it short (under about 70 characters) and true to the footage.

title: Two-font hierarchy
find: font pairing typography hierarchy weight size
body: One heavy display face for emphasis, one clean face for support. Size and weight show importance; more than two families looks accidental. Fonts must be bundled with the render (offline).

title: Sparing emoji accents
find: emoji sticker icon accent
body: A single emoji can mark a beat or soften a line. For financial advertising keep it rare and never imply guaranteed results with it.

title: Lower-third label
find: lower third name title label bar slide
body: A small slide-in card naming who is speaking or what is being discussed. Credibility on first appearance. Sits above the caption band and outside the face.

title: Stat card with count-up
find: number count up stat card dataviz big number
body: A big number with a short label that counts up as it is spoken. Only numbers the speaker says. Keep it on screen long enough to read (about 2-3 seconds) and clear of the face and captions.

title: Comparison split (A vs B)
find: comparison split before after side by side versus
body: Two panels contrasting two options or outcomes while the speaker compares them. Clear, simple labels; do not invent data.

title: Chart that draws on
find: chart line draw on svg path dataviz graph
body: An animated line or bars drawing on as the speaker explains a pattern (for trading content: price, a lagging indicator versus a leading one). Illustrative charts must be clearly illustrative, never presented as real results unless the data is real and approved.

title: Hand-drawn marker callout
find: callout arrow hand drawn marker annotation
body: A short note with an arrow popping near what the speaker points at. The current default look; keep the text to what is said. Varying its style (arrow, circle, underline, box) avoids sameness.

title: Pull-quote card
find: quote card pull quote text panel
body: Lift the line worth repeating into a large text card for a moment. Good for the thesis of the ad. Quote only the spoken words.

title: Progress or step bar
find: progress bar steps timeline indicator
body: A thin bar or step markers showing where the viewer is in a list or process; encourages watching to the end.

title: Picture-in-picture proof
find: picture in picture inset screenshot panel side panel
body: A small inset or side panel showing a screenshot, chart or demo while the speaker keeps talking. Needs assets from the client; never fabricate screenshots.

title: Grain, shimmer and texture finish
find: film grain shimmer texture overlay registry block
body: Light film grain or a gentle sheen unifies graphics and footage so overlays feel part of the image. Subtle only; heavy effects hurt legibility and file size.

title: End card with morphing button
find: cta morph press button end card pill
body: The closing card builds in: message, then a button that morphs and presses. A polished way to finish; its wording stays exactly as the owner set it.

title: Logo lockup end card
find: logo assemble lockup brand end card
body: Brand mark assembling with the call to action. Use when brand recognition matters more than a button.

title: Freeze-frame end card
find: freeze frame split end card text panel
body: Hold the last frame and slide in text on one side. Quiet and credible; works well with a calm speaker.

title: Level the loudness
find: loudnorm lufs loudness normalise audio level
body: Normalise speech to about -14 LUFS with a true-peak limit so every ad plays at a consistent level and never clips. ffmpeg's loudnorm does it; check the result by listening.

title: Clean up speech
find: denoise noise reduction afftdn highpass eq voice
body: A gentle high-pass and noise reduction removes room hum and hiss. Too much makes the voice watery; compare before and after.

title: Sound effects on cuts and graphics
find: sound effect whoosh hit sfx transition audio
body: A soft whoosh or tick on a graphic entrance or hard cut adds punch. Needs licensed sounds; keep levels well under the voice.

title: Music bed under the voice
find: music bed ducking background track volume duck voiceover
body: Low background music that drops further whenever the speaker talks. Adds mood; needs licensed music and careful levels so speech stays clear.

title: Light colour grade
find: color grade lut contrast saturation eq curves
body: A small lift in contrast and a consistent colour temperature makes phone footage look intentional. Subtle; never shift skin tones.

title: Reframe to vertical
find: crop reframe vertical subject tracking scale aspect
body: Fit the footage to 9:16 (or 4:5, 1:1) keeping the speaker centred; track movement when the source is wider. Currently a centre crop, so a speaker off-centre in a wide source loses framing.

title: Aspect-ratio variants
find: aspect ratio 4:5 1:1 9:16 safe zone variants
body: Deliver the same ad as 9:16, 4:5 and 1:1. Overlays and captions must be placed per format, not just cropped.

title: On-screen claims must be spoken
find: claim compliance disclosure numbers percent guarantee
body: Every number, percentage or promise that appears as text or a graphic must be said by the speaker in the ad. Never imply guaranteed returns. Flag anything a financial-ad reviewer could question and leave the decision to a person.

title: Standard risk/disclosure line
find: disclosure risk disclaimer line compliance text
body: A short standard risk line in the ad copy (and sometimes on the end card) for investing content. The wording comes from the owner's compliance reviewer, not from the AI.
